Abstract:

The exponential growth of the internet has intensified malware threats, affecting 26.3% of devices according to the 2023 Kaspersky report, while AI detectors grapple with noisy mislabeled samples, bias, and concept drift. Moreover, IBM&rsquos 2023Data Breach Report highlights a 320-day average patching time costing $165 per vulnerability.&nbspTo counter mislabeling, the proposed PFMD employs a two-stage pipeline that dynamically analyzes system/API calls from PE files. These system/API calls are transformed into bag of n-grams or anomaly sequences. After applying filtering, PFMD achieves 0.62 MCC on Ember datasets with over 18,000 samples. To address concept drift in PEs, proposed CSMD augments categorical call sequences via Gibbs sampling and temporal n-gram binning. CSMD delivers 0.7781 classification MCC on 10,000 drifted samples. For vulnerability management, a blending model preprocesses vulnerability descriptions through cleaning, tokenization, and n-gram analysis. Then, the model selects impactful n-grams using CMFS/ICMFS/IGFSS and classifies via KNN/GB/RF/BERT. The model yields 0.81 MCC to map vulnerability descriptions to SDLC phases and speed patching. Finally, proposed MFSL-VulClass tackles CWE classification by &ldquomix&rdquo selecting correlated source code tokens. MFSL-VulClass processes tokens through 1D CNN for short-term dependencies and bi-RNN for long-term context, attaining 0.91 MCC on open-source C programs to prioritize mitigations. Together, these innovations strengthen malware detection, drift resilience, and vulnerability response.
